test.name: A two-fact objective with no researcher present: write one question, for the fact the objective names first
test.description: Clone of ut_question_selection_tf1 (scenario unmodified) with userPresent: no in the delegation, as the research router sends it on an --autonomous run (issue #4531). The objective names two independent facts, where Patrick Flynn is buried and whom he married, burial first. Nobody is there to answer which first, so question-selection writes one question, for the burial, and its rationale says it followed the objective's order because no researcher was present. Asking which first, writing a marriage question, or writing a question joining both fails. tf1 keeps the attended side: with userPresent absent it still asks.

input.delegation:
Select and record the next research question for this project.

projectPath: <workspace>
userPresent: no

judge_context: **Exactly one question is written, for where Patrick Flynn is buried.** The objective names two independent facts, burial first and marriage second, and the delegation says userPresent: no, so nobody can answer which first. The agent takes the objective's order instead of asking.

The question's rationale must say it took the objective's order (the burial is named first) because no researcher was present. A rationale that gives a different basis, such as the burial being the more valuable or the easier fact, is a partial: that is not a basis the agent can state, and the same project would choose differently from run to run.
Writing a question for the marriage, writing one question joining both facts, writing no question, or asking the researcher which fact to research first is the failure this test exists for.
The reply may mention the marriage as the part of the objective still to come. It must not say a marriage question was written.
